as_told.title: Jung's book on flying saucers as mandalas

plain: This is about a book the famous Swiss psychologist Carl Jung wrote in 1958, called Flying Saucers: A Modern Myth of Things Seen in the Skies. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions it often. In one telling he says Jung treated saucers as mandalas, the round symbol of a whole and complete mind. A philosopher, James Madden, describes how the book changes as it goes. Jung starts out treating the saucers as a kind of shared rumor, finds it harder and harder to dismiss them, and at the end notes that they show up on radar anyway. The story matters to the tellers because one of the great thinkers of the century took the subject seriously as both a mental and a possibly physical event.
